title: WAN Technologies: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Your company has offices in different cities. How do their networks talk to each other? That's the job of a wide area network.

scenes.heading: Intercity rail lines
scenes.narration: Think of each office network as a city's local streets. A WAN is the railway line between cities. Leased lines like T one and T three are private tracks you rent. MPLS is a managed express service run by a provider. And a V P N rides the public internet, with a locked tunnel.

items.real: IPsec or SSL over the internet

scenes.heading: Speeds to know
scenes.narration: Memorise a few numbers. A T one carries twenty four channels of sixty four kilobits. A T three is about forty four megabits. E one is two megabits, used outside North America. O C three is about a hundred and fifty five megabits.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Watch for these. I P sec uses U D P five hundred and forty five hundred, not T C P. S S L V P N uses T C P four four three. And M P L S sits between layer two and three.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva WAN technologies lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. A WAN joins sites together, using leased lines, M P L S or V P N. T one is one point five four four megabits. I P sec uses U D P five hundred, and S S L uses T C P four four three. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva WAN technologies lab.
